content.title: pinch - Wiktionary, the free dictionary
content.text: From Wiktionary, the free dictionary From Middle English pinchen, from Old Northern French *pinchier (compare Old French pincier, pincer (“to pinch”)), a word of uncertain origin, possibly from Vulgar Latin *pinciāre (“to puncture, pinch”), from a merger of *punctiāre (“to puncture, sting”), from Latin punctiō (“a puncture, prick”) and *piccāre (“to strike, sting”), from Frankish *pikkōn, from Proto-Germanic *pikkōną (“to pick, peck, prick”). More at point, pick and pitch. IPA(key): /pɪnt͡ʃ/ Audio (US):Duration: 2 seconds.(file) Rhymes: -ɪntʃ pinch (third-person singular simple present pinches, present participle pinching, simple past and past participle pinched) To squeeze a small amount of a person's skin and flesh, making it hurt. The children were scolded for pinching each other. This shoe pinches my foot. To squeeze between the thumb and forefinger. quotations ▼ To squeeze between two objects. quotations ▼ (intransitive) Of clothing, to be uncomfortably tight in specific spots. quotations ▼ (slang, transitive) To steal, usually something inconsequential. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: crib, purloin; see also Thesaurus:steal Someone has pinched my handkerchief! (slang, transitive) To arrest or capture. synonyms ▲Synonyms: bust, nick; see also Thesaurus:capture (horticulture) To cut shoots or buds of a plant in order to shape the plant, or to improve its yield. (nautical) To sail so close-hauled that the sails begin to flutter. (hunting) To take hold; to grip, as a dog does. (obsolete, intransitive) To be stingy or covetous; to live sparingly. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: cheesepare, cut it fine, pinch pennies, skimp (of animals) To seize; to grip; to bite. quotations ▼ (figurative) To cramp; to straiten; to oppress; to starve. quotations ▼to be pinched for money To move, as a railroad car, by prying the wheels with a pinch. (obsolete) To complain or find fault. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: grumble, rail; see also Thesaurus:complain apinchbepinchpenny-pinchpinchabilitypinchablepinch a loafpinch atpinch-belly vengeancepinchcockpincherpinch-eyedpinchfistpinchfistedpinch-me-roundpinch-nose glassespinch offpinch one offpinch outpinch penniespinchpennysquinchtopinchunpinch show ▼±to squeeze a small amount of skin show ▼±horticulture: to cut shoots or buds show ▼±nautical: to sail close-hauled show ▼Translations to be checked pinch (plural pinches) The action of squeezing a small amount of a person's skin and flesh, making it hurt. A close compression of anything with the fingers. I gave the leather of the sofa a pinch, gauging the texture. A small amount of powder or granules, such that the amount could be held between fingertip and thumb tip. synonyms ▲Synonyms: smidgen; see also Thesaurus:modicum Mix about four cups of white flour with a pinch of salt. An awkward situation of some kind (especially money or social) which is difficult to escape. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: difficulty, kettle of fish; see also Thesaurus:difficult situation A metal bar used as a lever for lifting weights, rolling wheels, etc. synonyms ▲Synonyms: crowbar, jimmy, nail bar An organic herbal smoke additive. (physics) A magnetic compression of an electrically conducting filament. The narrow part connecting the two bulbs of an hourglass. quotations ▼ (slang) An arrest. synonyms ▲Synonyms: bust, collar (Australia, New Zealand) A steep incline; a very steep section of road. quotations ▼ at a pinchBennett pinchcock-and-pinchfeel the pinchin a pinchJack at a pinchnanopinchon a pinchpinch and a punch for the first of the monthpinch bar, pinchbarpinch-bellypinch cakepinch-commonspinch effectpinch forcepinch graftingpinch-gutpinch-hitpinch hitpinch hitterpinch-hitterpinchlikepinch of saltpinch of the gamepinch pointpinch potpinch rollerpinch runnerpinchyQueens Pinchtake with a pinch of salttheta pinchvelar pinchYellow Pinchzeta pinchZ-pinchθ-pinch → Japanese: ピンチ (pinchi) show ▼±action of squeezing a small amount of skin
